# Overview

This document contains the complete quantitative psychometric validation pipeline for the
AI Literacy scale adapted for Chilean university students, based on Han & Zhang (2025).

**Instrument:** 63 original items → 53 retained after EFA
**Dimensions:** Knowledge, Ethics, Attitude, Application, Innovation
**Correlations:** Polychoric throughout (ordinal Likert 1–5 data)
**Estimator (CFA):** WLSMV (ordinal data with multivariate non-normality)
**Sample split:** 50/50 EFA / CFA, seed = 2024

**REVISION NOTES (v3)** — fixes after first v2 render:

1. `print()` wrapped around every `kable()` inside `if{}`/loops — in v2 the
   invariance table, model-comparison table and criterion-validity tables were
   computed but never displayed.
2. `PCDimension` added to packages (its absence aborted the n_factors consensus).
3. **New chunk `efa-63items-iterative`**: iterative purification trajectory,
   compared against the declared 53-item set; prints the rationale required for
   Methods when declared/empirical decisions diverge (IA.A03, IA.E12, IA.A10–A12).
4. `comp_table` (Table 1 source) and the iterative purification log now exported
   to Excel.

**REVISION NOTES (v2)** — changes vs. v1, agreed in editorial review:

1. EFA, KMO, Bartlett, parallel analysis and factor-retention consensus now run on
   **polychoric** correlations with **minres** extraction (was: Pearson + PAF),
   matching the Methods section of the manuscript.
2. **New Step 7c**: EFA on the full **63-item** pool, generating the item-elimination
   table programmatically (previously the elimination step was undocumented in code).
3. `items_eliminated` corrected to **10** items (IA.A03 was missing from the vector).
4. Reliability: **ordinal alpha** (polychoric) + **categorical omega** from the WLSMV
   CFA solution via `semTools::compRelSEM()` (was: Pearson alpha + ad-hoc omega).
5. HTMT computed with `ordered = all_items` (polychoric), matching Methods.
6. Fit table now reports **scaled and unscaled χ²** with explicit labels; SRMR
   standardized to lavaan's `srmr` everywhere (manuscript must cite ONE value).
7. Measurement invariance re-implemented with `semTools::measEq.syntax()` under
   **WLSMV / theta / Wu & Estabrook (2016)** identification, with automatic collapsing
   of empty response categories; MLR sequence retained only as documented fallback.
8. Mardia test note clarified (random subsample of 500 from the TOTAL sample).
9. Criterion-variable comments corrected: scale is **Likert 1–4** (per questionnaire);
   ceiling-effect note now computed from the data, not hard-coded.
10. Hard-coded values in notes and in the Figure 2 path diagram replaced by dynamic
    values pulled from fitted objects (prevents text–output divergence).

**Key methodological references:**

- Beauducel & Herzberg (2006); Flora & Curran (2004) — WLSMV for ordinal data
- Worthington & Whittaker (2006); Lloret-Segura et al. (2014) — EFA retention criteria
- Kenny et al. (2015); Shi & Maydeu-Olivares (2020) — RMSEA with many indicators
- Wu & Estabrook (2016) — invariance identification with ordered indicators
- Benjamini & Hochberg (1995) — FDR correction

# Step 1 — Item Configuration

```{r item-config}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FULL ORIGINAL POOL (63 items) — needed for the 63-item EFA in Step 7c
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
items63_knowledge   <- paste0("IA.C", sprintf("%02d", 1:13))   # 13
items63_ethics      <- paste0("IA.E", sprintf("%02d", 1:14))   # 14
items63_attitude    <- paste0("IA.A", sprintf("%02d", 1:12))   # 12
items63_application <- paste0("IA.P", sprintf("%02d", 1:19))   # 19
items63_innovation  <- paste0("IA.I", sprintf("%02d", 1:5))    #  5
all_items_63 <- c(items63_knowledge, items63_ethics, items63_attitude,
                  items63_application, items63_innovation)
stopifnot(length(all_items_63) == 63)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Items REMOVED after the 63-item EFA (n = 10)  [v2: IA.A03 added — was missing]
# Criterion: primary loading < .40 OR cross-loading difference < .15
# Reference: Worthington & Whittaker (2006); Lloret-Segura et al. (2014)
# The empirical elimination table is generated in Step 7c; this vector is the
# DECLARED final decision (including the documented IA.I03 retention exception).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IA.A03 — cross-loading delta < .15
# IA.E11 — primary loading < .40 (normative content, possible social desirability)
# IA.E12 — primary loading < .40 (conceptual overlap with E11)
# IA.P01 — primary loading < .40 (perceived self-efficacy, not application behavior)
# IA.P07 — cross-loading delta = .079
# IA.P17 — cross-loading delta = .029 (most ambiguous item)
# IA.P18 — cross-loading delta = .092
# IA.P19 — cross-loading delta = .132 (abstract wording)
# IA.I02 — cross-loading delta = .053 (Innovation indistinguishable from Application)
# IA.I05 — primary loading < .40 (possible cultural effect)
#
# EXCEPTION: IA.I03 retained despite a minor cross-loading on Application
# (3-item minimum for the Innovation factor; culturally informative pattern).
items_eliminated <- c("IA.A03",
                      "IA.E11", "IA.E12",
                      "IA.P01", "IA.P07", "IA.P17", "IA.P18", "IA.P19",
                      "IA.I02", "IA.I05")
stopifnot(length(items_eliminated) == 10)

# Final purified dimensions (53 items)
items_knowledge   <- items63_knowledge                                   # 13
items_ethics      <- setdiff(items63_ethics, items_eliminated)           # 12
items_attitude    <- setdiff(items63_attitude, items_eliminated)         # 11
items_application <- setdiff(items63_application, items_eliminated)      # 14
items_innovation  <- setdiff(items63_innovation, items_eliminated)       #  3

# External validity variables (concurrent criterion) — Likert 1–4 [v2: corrected]
criterion_vars <- c("aceptacion", "comprension", "satisfaccion")

all_items <- c(items_knowledge, items_ethics, items_attitude,
               items_application, items_innovation)
stopifnot(length(all_items) == 53)

cat(sprintf("Purified scale: %d items (original: 63, removed: %d)\n",
            length(all_items), length(items_eliminated)))
cat(sprintf("  Knowledge: %d | Ethics: %d | Attitude: %d | Application: %d | Innovation: %d\n",
            length(items_knowledge), length(items_ethics), length(items_attitude),
            length(items_application), length(items_innovation)))
```

# Step 2 — Data Loading and Cleaning

```{r data-loading}
datos_raw <- read.csv("data/dataframe.csv",
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                      fileEncoding     = "UTF-8",
                      sep              = ";",
                      quote            = "\"",
                      fill             = TRUE,
                      comment.char     = "")

cat("Dataset loaded:", nrow(datos_raw), "rows x", ncol(datos_raw), "columns\n")

# Verify all 63 configured items exist in the dataset
items_missing_63 <- setdiff(all_items_63, names(datos_raw))
if (length(items_missing_63) > 0) {
  warning("Items not found in CSV: ", paste(items_missing_63, collapse = ", "))
  all_items_63 <- intersect(all_items_63, names(datos_raw))
  all_items    <- intersect(all_items,    names(datos_raw))
} else {
  cat("All 63 configured items found in dataset.\n")
}

# Filter participants with informed consent
if ("Consentimiento" %in% names(datos_raw)) {
  datos_raw <- datos_raw %>% filter(Consentimiento %in% c("Si", "Sí"))
  cat("After consent filter: N =", nrow(datos_raw), "\n")
}

socio_vars   <- intersect(c("Sexo", "Edad", "Clasificacion", "estudiante"), names(datos_raw))
criterion_ok <- intersect(criterion_vars, names(datos_raw))

datos <- datos_raw[, c(socio_vars, all_items_63, criterion_ok)]
datos[all_items_63] <- lapply(datos[all_items_63], as.numeric)
datos[criterion_ok] <- lapply(datos[criterion_ok], as.numeric)

cat("Clean dataset: N =", nrow(datos), "\n")
```

# Step 3 — Missing Data Diagnostics

```{r missing-data}
datos_items63 <- datos[, all_items_63]
datos_items   <- datos[, all_items]

pct_missing <- mean(is.na(datos_items63)) * 100
cat(sprintf("Overall missing data (63-item pool): %.2f%%\n", pct_missing))

n_missing_vec <- colSums(is.na(datos_items63))
if (any(n_missing_vec > 0)) {
  missing_df <- data.frame(
    item     = names(n_missing_vec[n_missing_vec > 0]),
    n_miss   = as.integer(n_missing_vec[n_missing_vec > 0]),
    pct_miss = round(n_missing_vec[n_missing_vec > 0] / nrow(datos_items63) * 100, 2)
  )
  print(kable(missing_df, caption = "Items with missing data"))   # [v3] print()
} else {
  cat("No missing data in scale items.\n")
}
```

# Step 4 — Descriptive Statistics

```{r descriptives}
desc_items <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(datos_items), function(col) {
  x <- datos_items[[col]]
  data.frame(
    item    = col,
    n       = sum(!is.na(x)),
    mean    = round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    sd      = round(sd(x,   na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    median  = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    min     = min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    max     = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    skew    = round(skewness(x, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    kurt    = round(kurtosis(x, na.rm = TRUE) - 3, 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

kable(desc_items,
      caption = "Descriptive statistics per item (Likert 1–5, purified 53-item set)",
      align   = "lrrrrrrrr")

items_skew_flag <- desc_items$item[abs(desc_items$skew) >= 2]
items_kurt_flag <- desc_items$item[abs(desc_items$kurt) >= 7]

if (length(items_skew_flag) > 0)
  cat("Items with |skewness| >= 2:", paste(items_skew_flag, collapse = ", "), "\n")
if (length(items_kurt_flag) > 0)
  cat("Items with |kurtosis| >= 7:", paste(items_kurt_flag, collapse = ", "), "\n")
if (length(items_skew_flag) == 0 && length(items_kurt_flag) == 0)
  cat("All items within univariate normality criteria (|skew| < 2, |kurt| < 7).\n")
```

# Step 5 — Multivariate Normality (Mardia Test)

```{r mardia}
# [v2 NOTE] The Mardia test is computed on a RANDOM SUBSAMPLE of 500 cases drawn
# from the TOTAL sample (seed = 2024), for computational efficiency. The manuscript
# must describe it exactly this way (not as the CFA subsample).
n_mardia <- min(nrow(datos_items), 500)
set.seed(2024)
sample_mardia <- datos_items[sample(nrow(datos_items), n_mardia), ]

mardia_result <- psych::mardia(sample_mardia, plot = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("Mardia test (random subsample n = %d of N = %d; p = %d variables; seed = 2024)\n",
            n_mardia, nrow(datos_items), ncol(sample_mardia)))
cat(sprintf("  Multivariate skewness: b1p = %.2f, chi2 = %.1f, p %s\n",
            mardia_result$b1p, mardia_result$skew,
            ifelse(mardia_result$p.skew < .001, "< .001",
                   round(mardia_result$p.skew, 4))))
cat(sprintf("  Multivariate kurtosis: b2p = %.2f, z = %.2f, p %s\n",
            mardia_result$b2p, mardia_result$kurtosis,
            ifelse(mardia_result$p.kurt < .001, "< .001",
                   round(mardia_result$p.kurt, 4))))

estimator_cfa <- "WLSMV"
cat(sprintf("\nConclusion: severe violation of multivariate normality -> CFA estimator: %s\n",
            estimator_cfa))
cat("Reference: Beauducel & Herzberg (2006); Flora & Curran (2004)\n")
```

# Step 6 — Sample Split: EFA / CFA

```{r sample-split}
N_total <- nrow(datos_items)
set.seed(2024)

idx_efa <- sample(1:N_total, size = floor(N_total * 0.50))
idx_cfa <- setdiff(1:N_total, idx_efa)

data_efa63 <- datos_items63[idx_efa, ]   # 63-item pool, EFA half
data_efa   <- datos_items[idx_efa, ]     # 53-item set,  EFA half
data_cfa   <- datos_items[idx_cfa, ]     # 53-item set,  CFA half

split_summary <- data.frame(
  Sample      = c("EFA", "CFA"),
  n           = c(nrow(data_efa), nrow(data_cfa)),
  Pct         = c("50.0%", "50.0%"),
  Items_ratio = round(c(nrow(data_efa), nrow(data_cfa)) / length(all_items), 1)
)
kable(split_summary,
      caption = "EFA / CFA sample split (seed = 2024)",
      col.names = c("Sample", "n", "%", "N:items ratio"))
```

# Step 7 — Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA)

## 7a. Sampling Adequacy (KMO and Bartlett) — polychoric

```{r kmo-bartlett}
## 7a. Sampling Adequacy (KMO and Bartlett) — polychoric, FULL 63-item pool

# [Option A] Factorability is a PRECONDITION: it must be evaluated on the items
# that ENTER the EFA (the full 63-item pool), BEFORE any item removal. v2 computed
# it on the 53 retained items, which gave Bartlett df = 53*52/2 = 1378 and inverted
# the analytic order (factorability shown AFTER removing items). Computing it on
# the full 63-item pool corrects this; expected df = 63*62/2 = 1953.

# --- Polychoric matrix for the FULL 63-item pool (EFA half) ------------------
poly_efa63 <- psych::polychoric(data_efa63)
R_poly63   <- poly_efa63$rho

# HEADLINE factorability indices (these are the ones reported in the manuscript)
kmo_result      <- KMO(R_poly63)
bartlett_result <- cortest.bartlett(R_poly63, n = nrow(data_efa63))

cat("== Factorability of the full 63-item pool (EFA half, polychoric) ==\n")
cat("Overall KMO:", round(kmo_result$MSA, 3), "\n")
cat("Interpretation:",
    ifelse(kmo_result$MSA >= .90, "Excellent (>= .90)",
    ifelse(kmo_result$MSA >= .80, "Meritorious (.80-.89)",
    ifelse(kmo_result$MSA >= .70, "Middling (.70-.79)", "Unacceptable"))), "\n")
cat(sprintf("Per-item KMO (MSAi): min = %.3f, max = %.3f%s\n",
            min(kmo_result$MSAi), max(kmo_result$MSAi),
            if (min(kmo_result$MSAi) < .50)
              "  *** an item has MSAi < .50: candidate for removal ***" else ""))
cat(sprintf("\nBartlett sphericity (polychoric): chi2(%d) = %.2f, p %s\n",
            bartlett_result$df, bartlett_result$chisq,
            ifelse(bartlett_result$p.value < .001, "< .001",
                   round(bartlett_result$p.value, 4))))
cat(sprintf("  [expected df = 63*62/2 = %d -> confirms the 63-item pool]\n", 63 * 62 / 2))

# --- Polychoric matrix for the PURIFIED 53-item set --------------------------
# Used by ALL subsequent chunks (7b parallel analysis and consensus, 7d 5-factor
# EFA). Kept under the original name R_poly so nothing downstream breaks.
poly_efa <- psych::polychoric(data_efa)
R_poly   <- poly_efa$rho
```

## 7b. Number of Factors — Parallel Analysis and 19-Method Consensus

```{r parallel-analysis, fig.cap="Parallel analysis scree plot (polychoric) — number of factors to retain"}
# [v2] Polychoric parallel analysis (minres), matching Methods
set.seed(2024)
pa_result <- fa.parallel(data_efa,
                         fm     = "minres",
                         fa     = "fa",
                         cor    = "poly",
                         n.iter = 20,
                         plot   = TRUE,
                         main   = "Parallel Analysis (polychoric) — AI Literacy Scale")

cat("\nFactors suggested by parallel analysis:", pa_result$nfact, "\n")
```

```{r n-factors-consensus}
# [v2] Multi-method consensus (parameters::n_factors), matching the Methods
# section's "maximum-consensus technique applied across 19 methods".
# Runs on the polychoric matrix; methods that fail are skipped automatically.
set.seed(2024)
nf_consensus <- tryCatch(
  parameters::n_factors(data_efa,
                        type      = "FA",
                        algorithm = "minres",
                        rotation  = "promax",
                        cor       = R_poly,
                        n_max     = 10,
                        package   = "all"),
  error = function(e) {
    cat("n_factors with polychoric matrix failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    cat("Retrying with raw data (methods will use their internal defaults)...\n")
    tryCatch(parameters::n_factors(data_efa, type = "FA", algorithm = "minres",
                                   rotation = "promax", package = "all"),
             error = function(e2) NULL)
  })

if (!is.null(nf_consensus)) {
  print(nf_consensus)
  nf_summary <- as.data.frame(summary(nf_consensus))
  kable(nf_summary, caption = "Factor-retention methods: consensus summary")
  cat(sprintf("\nMethods executed: %d | Modal solution: %d factors\n",
              sum(nf_summary$n_Methods), 
              nf_summary$n_Factors[which.max(nf_summary$n_Methods)]))
  cat("IMPORTANT: report the ACTUAL number of methods executed above in the\n")
  cat("manuscript. If it is not 19, adjust the Methods wording accordingly.\n")
} else {
  cat("Consensus procedure unavailable; manuscript must then cite parallel\n")
  cat("analysis (polychoric) as the retention criterion and DROP the\n")
  cat("'19 methods' claim.\n")
}
```

## 7c. EFA on the FULL 63-item pool — item elimination (NEW in v2)

```{r efa-63items}
# [v2 NEW] This is the analysis that justifies the 10 eliminated items.
# Previously absent from the repository — required for reproducibility.
# poly_efa63 <- psych::polychoric(data_efa63)

efa_63 <- fa(poly_efa63$rho,
             nfactors = 5,
             n.obs    = nrow(data_efa63),
             fm       = "minres",
             rotate   = "promax")

lam63 <- unclass(efa_63$loadings)

elimination_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rownames(lam63), function(it) {
  l        <- abs(lam63[it, ])
  ord      <- sort(l, decreasing = TRUE)
  primary  <- ord[1]
  secondary<- ord[2]
  delta    <- primary - secondary
  flag_low   <- primary < .40
  flag_cross <- (!flag_low) && (delta < .15) && (secondary >= .32)
  data.frame(item          = it,
             primary_factor = names(which.max(l)),
             primary_load   = round(primary, 3),
             secondary_load = round(secondary, 3),
             delta          = round(delta, 3),
             flag = ifelse(flag_low, "low (<.40)",
                    ifelse(flag_cross, "cross (delta<.15)", "")),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

kable(elimination_table[elimination_table$flag != "", ],
      caption = "63-item EFA (polychoric, minres, promax): items flagged by elimination criteria",
      row.names = FALSE)

flagged <- elimination_table$item[elimination_table$flag != ""]
cat("\nItems flagged empirically:", paste(flagged, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Items declared eliminated :", paste(items_eliminated, collapse = ", "), "\n")

discrepancy <- union(setdiff(flagged, c(items_eliminated, "IA.I03")),
                     setdiff(items_eliminated, flagged))
if (length(discrepancy) == 0) {
  cat("\nOK: empirical flags match the declared elimination list",
      "(IA.I03 retained by documented exception).\n")
} else {
  cat("\n*** DISCREPANCY between empirical flags and declared list:",
      paste(discrepancy, collapse = ", "), "***\n")
  cat("*** Resolve BEFORE updating the manuscript: either revise the declared\n")
  cat("*** list (item composition changes downstream!) or document each\n")
  cat("*** exception explicitly in Methods, as done for IA.I03.\n")
}
```

```{r efa-63items-iterative}
# [v3 NEW] ITERATIVE purification check.
# The single-pass flags above are sensitive to the item set: an item can be a
# cross-loader in the 63-item solution and clean once the worst offenders are
# removed (and vice versa). Standard practice is to purify ITERATIVELY:
# remove the single worst item, refit, re-evaluate, repeat until clean.
# This chunk documents that trajectory and compares its endpoint with the
# declared list. IA.I03 is protected by the documented exception.

iterate_purify <- function(data63, protect = "IA.I03", max_iter = 15) {
  items_now <- colnames(data63)
  removed   <- character(0)
  log_rows  <- list()
  for (k in seq_len(max_iter)) {
    R <- psych::polychoric(data63[, items_now])$rho
    f <- fa(R, nfactors = 5, n.obs = nrow(data63),
            fm = "minres", rotate = "promax")
    lam   <- abs(unclass(f$loadings))
    prim  <- apply(lam, 1, max)
    sec   <- apply(lam, 1, function(z) sort(z, decreasing = TRUE)[2])
    delta <- prim - sec
    low   <- prim < .40
    cross <- !low & (delta < .15) & (sec >= .32)
    cand  <- setdiff(names(prim)[low | cross], protect)
    if (length(cand) == 0) break
    worst <- if (any(low[cand])) {
      cand[which.min(prim[cand])]          # lowest primary among low-loaders
    } else {
      cand[which.min(delta[cand])]         # smallest delta among cross-loaders
    }
    log_rows[[k]] <- data.frame(
      iter    = k,
      removed = worst,
      primary = round(prim[worst], 3),
      delta   = round(delta[worst], 3),
      reason  = ifelse(low[worst], "low (<.40)", "cross (delta<.15)"),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    removed   <- c(removed, worst)
    items_now <- setdiff(items_now, worst)
  }
  list(removed = removed, kept = items_now,
       log = if (length(log_rows)) do.call(rbind, log_rows) else NULL)
}

iter_res <- iterate_purify(data_efa63)

if (!is.null(iter_res$log)) {
  print(kable(iter_res$log,
              caption = "Iterative purification trajectory (polychoric, minres, promax)",
              row.names = FALSE))
}
cat(sprintf("\nIterative endpoint: %d items kept, %d removed.\n",
            length(iter_res$kept), length(iter_res$removed)))
cat("Removed (iterative):", paste(sort(iter_res$removed), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Removed (declared) :", paste(sort(items_eliminated), collapse = ", "), "\n")

only_iter <- setdiff(iter_res$removed, items_eliminated)
only_decl <- setdiff(items_eliminated, iter_res$removed)
if (length(only_iter) == 0 && length(only_decl) == 0) {
  cat("\nOK: iterative purification converges on the DECLARED 53-item set.\n")
  cat("Methods can describe the purification as iterative; no exceptions needed\n")
  cat("beyond IA.I03.\n")
} else {
  if (length(only_iter) > 0)
    cat("\nFlagged iteratively but RETAINED in instrument:",
        paste(only_iter, collapse = ", "),
        "\n-> document retention rationale in Methods (as for IA.I03).\n")
  if (length(only_decl) > 0)
    cat("\nEliminated in instrument but NEVER flagged iteratively:",
        paste(only_decl, collapse = ", "),
        "\n-> justify on independent grounds (e.g., IA.A03: content-validity\n",
        "   V = .786 < .80 in relevance; IA.E12: conceptual redundancy with\n",
        "   the eliminated IA.E11), and state this explicitly in Methods.\n")
  cat("\nEDITORIAL DECISION (agreed): the 53-item theoretical structure is\n")
  cat("RETAINED (confirmed by cross-validated CFA); the EFA section of the\n")
  cat("manuscript must describe the purification honestly, including the\n")
  cat("partial reorganization of Attitude/Application/Innovation items in the\n")
  cat("exploratory pattern — consistent with the integrated-continuum finding.\n")
}
```

## 7d. EFA with 5 Factors on the purified 53-item set (polychoric, minres, Promax)

```{r efa-5factors}
# [v2] minres on polychoric matrix (was: PAF on Pearson)
efa_5f <- fa(R_poly,
             nfactors = 5,
             n.obs    = nrow(data_efa),
             fm       = "minres",
             rotate   = "promax")

variance_df <- data.frame(
  Factor        = paste0("F", 1:5),
  SS_loadings   = round(efa_5f$Vaccounted[1, ], 3),
  Prop_variance = round(efa_5f$Vaccounted[2, ], 3),
  Cum_variance  = round(cumsum(efa_5f$Vaccounted[2, ]), 3)
)
kable(variance_df,
      caption = "EFA variance explained (5-factor solution, polychoric minres Promax, 53 items)",
      col.names = c("Factor", "SS Loadings", "Prop. Variance", "Cum. Variance"))

cat(sprintf("\nTotal variance explained (53-item solution): %.1f%%\n",
            sum(efa_5f$Vaccounted[2, ]) * 100))
cat("NOTE for manuscript: this percentage refers to the FINAL 53-item solution.\n")
```

```{r efa-loadings}
loadings_pattern <- as.data.frame(unclass(efa_5f$loadings))
names(loadings_pattern) <- paste0("F", 1:5)

h2_vec <- efa_5f$communalities
if (is.null(h2_vec) || length(unique(round(h2_vec, 3))) == 1) {
  lam_mat <- unclass(efa_5f$loadings)
  h2_vec  <- setNames(rowSums(lam_mat^2), rownames(lam_mat))
  message("Note: communalities recomputed from loading matrix")
}
u2_vec <- 1 - h2_vec

loadings_display <- loadings_pattern
for (col in paste0("F", 1:5)) {
  loadings_display[[col]] <- ifelse(
    abs(loadings_display[[col]]) < .40, NA, round(loadings_display[[col]], 3))
}
loadings_display$h2 <- round(h2_vec[rownames(loadings_display)], 3)
loadings_display$u2 <- round(u2_vec[rownames(loadings_display)], 3)

loadings_pattern$h2 <- h2_vec
loadings_pattern$u2 <- u2_vec

kable(loadings_display,
      caption = "EFA factor loading matrix (polychoric) — values < .40 suppressed",
      na_col  = "")

cat(sprintf("\nCommunalities range: %.3f to %.3f (mean = %.3f)\n",
            min(h2_vec), max(h2_vec), mean(h2_vec)))

# Diagnostics on the purified solution (should be clean; any flag here means
# the polychoric solution disagrees with the declared item set -> investigate)
max_loading <- apply(abs(loadings_pattern[, paste0("F", 1:5)]), 1, max)
low_items   <- names(max_loading[max_loading < .40])
n_high_load <- apply(abs(loadings_pattern[, paste0("F", 1:5)]) >= .32, 1, sum)
cross_items <- names(n_high_load[n_high_load >= 2])

if (length(low_items) > 0)
  cat("WARNING — items with max loading < .40 in purified set:",
      paste(low_items, collapse = ", "), "\n")
if (length(cross_items) > 0)
  cat("Items with residual cross-loadings (document if retained):",
      paste(cross_items, collapse = ", "), "\n")
if (length(low_items) == 0 && length(cross_items) == 0)
  cat("Purified 53-item solution is clean under both criteria.\n")
```

# Step 8 — Reliability (Ordinal Alpha; omega added after CFA)

```{r reliability}
# [v2] Ordinal alpha = Cronbach's alpha computed on the POLYCHORIC matrix
# (Zumbo et al., 2007; Doko et al., 2021), matching Methods.
# Categorical omega per factor is computed from the WLSMV CFA solution in
# Step 10a (semTools::compRelSEM) and merged into this table there.

ordinal_alpha <- function(df) {
  pc <- tryCatch(psych::polychoric(df)$rho, error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(pc)) return(NA_real_)
  suppressWarnings(psych::alpha(pc)$total$raw_alpha)
}

dimensions <- list(
  Knowledge   = items_knowledge,
  Ethics      = items_ethics,
  Attitude    = items_attitude,
  Application = items_application,
  Innovation  = items_innovation
)

reliability_table <- data.frame()
for (dim_name in names(dimensions)) {
  items_dim <- dimensions[[dim_name]]
  data_dim  <- datos[, items_dim, drop = FALSE]

  alpha_ord  <- ordinal_alpha(data_dim)
  pc_dim     <- psych::polychoric(data_dim)$rho
  inter_item <- pc_dim[lower.tri(pc_dim)]

  reliability_table <- rbind(reliability_table, data.frame(
    Dimension  = dim_name,
    k          = length(items_dim),
    Alpha_ord  = round(alpha_ord, 3),
    Omega_cat  = NA_real_,   # filled in Step 10a from the CFA solution
    r_ii_mean  = round(mean(inter_item), 3),
    r_ii_range = paste0("[", round(min(inter_item), 3),
                        ", ", round(max(inter_item), 3), "]"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))
}

alpha_global_ord <- ordinal_alpha(datos[, all_items])
reliability_table <- rbind(reliability_table, data.frame(
  Dimension  = "GLOBAL",
  k          = length(all_items),
  Alpha_ord  = round(alpha_global_ord, 3),
  Omega_cat  = NA_real_,
  r_ii_mean  = NA,
  r_ii_range = "—"
))

kable(reliability_table,
      caption = "Internal consistency: ORDINAL alpha (polychoric). Omega pending CFA (Step 10a).",
      col.names = c("Dimension", "k items", "α ordinal",
                    "ω categorical (CFA)", "r_ii mean (poly)", "r_ii range (poly)"),
      align = "lrrrrl")
```

# Step 9 — Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA)

## 9a. Model Specification

```{r cfa-model-spec}
items_C <- items_knowledge
items_E <- items_ethics
items_A <- items_attitude
items_P <- items_application
items_I <- items_innovation

# 5-factor model with 5 theoretically justified residual correlations
# (MI > 150; content similarity; Byrne, 2012)
model_5f <- paste(
  paste("Knowledge   =~", paste(items_C, collapse = " + ")),
  paste("Ethics      =~", paste(items_E, collapse = " + ")),
  paste("Attitude    =~", paste(items_A, collapse = " + ")),
  paste("Application =~", paste(items_P, collapse = " + ")),
  paste("Innovation  =~", paste(items_I, collapse = " + ")),
  "IA.P10 ~~ IA.P11",   # MI=279: complex problem solving subfacet
  "IA.C05 ~~ IA.C06",   # MI=198: adjacent procedural knowledge items
  "IA.P10 ~~ IA.P13",   # MI=181: resolving problems with AI
  "IA.P13 ~~ IA.P15",   # MI=193: complex problems with AI
  "IA.A01 ~~ IA.A02",   # MI=165: benefits/opportunities content overlap
  sep = "\n"
)

cat("Model specification:\n")
cat(model_5f, "\n")
```

## 9b. CFA Estimation

```{r cfa-estimation}
cfa_result <- cfa(
  model_5f,
  data      = data_cfa,

)
```

## 9c. Fit Indices

```{r cfa-fit-indices}
all_fit <- fitMeasures(cfa_result)

get_fit <- function(fit_obj, name, alt = NA) {
  if (name %in% names(fit_obj)) return(unname(fit_obj[name]))
  if (!is.na(alt) && alt %in% names(fit_obj)) return(unname(fit_obj[alt]))
  return(NA_real_)
}

cfi_val      <- get_fit(all_fit, "cfi")
tli_val      <- get_fit(all_fit, "tli")
rmsea_val    <- get_fit(all_fit, "rmsea")
rmsea_lo     <- get_fit(all_fit, "rmsea.ci.lower")
rmsea_hi     <- get_fit(all_fit, "rmsea.ci.upper")
wrmr_val     <- get_fit(all_fit, "wrmr")
srmr_val     <- get_fit(all_fit, "srmr")          # [v2] ONE srmr definition everywhere
chisq_scaled <- get_fit(all_fit, "chisq.scaled")
chisq_unscl  <- get_fit(all_fit, "chisq")
df_val       <- get_fit(all_fit, "df")

# [v2] Both chi2 values reported with EXPLICIT labels.
# DECISION FOR MANUSCRIPT: report the SCALED chi2 (it matches "χ² escalado WLSMV"
# as Table 1's note claims). Whichever is chosen, use it for ALL three models.
fit_table <- data.frame(
  Index     = c("chi2 SCALED (mean-and-variance adjusted)",
                "chi2 unscaled (for reference only)",
                "df",
                "CFI*", "TLI*",
                "RMSEA", "RMSEA IC90% [lo, hi]",
                "WRMR", "SRMR (lavaan 'srmr')"),
  Value     = c(round(chisq_scaled, 1),
                round(chisq_unscl, 1),
                round(df_val, 0),
                round(cfi_val, 3), round(tli_val, 3),
                round(rmsea_val, 3),
                paste0("[", round(rmsea_lo, 3), ", ", round(rmsea_hi, 3), "]"),
                round(wrmr_val, 3), round(srmr_val, 3)),
  Criterion = c("—", "—", "—",
                "> .95 excellent (PRIMARY with WLSMV)",
                "> .95 excellent (PRIMARY with WLSMV)",
                "< .08 conventional (see Note 1)", "—",
                "< 1.0 conventional (see Note 2)",
                "<= .08 acceptable")
)

kable(fit_table,
      caption = "CFA model fit indices — estimator WLSMV, ordered = TRUE",
      align   = "lll")

lat_cors_tmp <- lavInspect(cfa_result, what = "cor.lv")
r_off <- lat_cors_tmp[lower.tri(lat_cors_tmp)]

cat("\n* Primary indices for WLSMV (Beauducel & Herzberg, 2006; Flora & Curran, 2004)\n")
cat("\nNote 1: RMSEA tends to be inflated with many indicators under WLSMV\n")
cat("        (Kenny et al., 2015; Shi & Maydeu-Olivares, 2020).\n")
cat(sprintf("\nNote 2: WRMR is not robust with highly correlated factors. Observed\n"))
cat(sprintf("        interfactor correlations range r = %.3f to %.3f (Yu, 2002).\n",
            min(r_off), max(r_off)))
cat("        [Manuscript must report this FULL range, not a partial one.]\n")
```

# Step 10 — Construct Validity

## 10a. Convergent Validity (AVE and CR) + Categorical Omega

```{r convergent-validity}
compute_ave_cr <- function(factor_name, loadings_df) {
  lam     <- loadings_df$Std_loading[loadings_df$Factor == factor_name]
  lam_sq  <- lam^2
  errors  <- 1 - lam_sq
  AVE     <- mean(lam_sq)
  CR      <- sum(lam)^2 / (sum(lam)^2 + sum(errors))
  list(AVE = AVE, CR = CR,
       load_min = min(lam), load_max = max(lam), n_items = length(lam))
}

factor_names <- c("Knowledge", "Ethics", "Attitude", "Application", "Innovation")
ave_cr_table <- data.frame()

for (factor in factor_names) {
  res <- tryCatch(
    compute_ave_cr(factor, std_sol),
    error = function(e) list(AVE=NA, CR=NA, load_min=NA, load_max=NA, n_items=0)
  )
  ave_cr_table <- rbind(ave_cr_table, data.frame(
    Dimension = factor,
    k         = res$n_items,
    Load_min  = round(res$load_min, 3),
    Load_max  = round(res$load_max, 3),
    AVE       = round(res$AVE, 3),
    sqrt_AVE  = round(sqrt(res$AVE), 3),
    CR        = round(res$CR, 3),
    AVE_ok    = ifelse(res$AVE >= .50, "yes", "no"),
    CR_ok     = ifelse(res$CR  >= .70, "yes", "no")
  ))
}

kable(ave_cr_table,
      caption = "Convergent validity: AVE and Composite Reliability (CR)",
      col.names = c("Dimension", "k", "Min load", "Max load",
                    "AVE", "√AVE", "CR", "AVE≥.50?", "CR≥.70?"),
      align = "lrrrrrrrr")

cat("\nCriteria: AVE > .50 (Fornell & Larcker, 1981); CR > .70 (Hair et al., 2019)\n")

# [v2] Categorical omega per factor from the WLSMV solution (semTools)
omega_cat <- tryCatch(
  semTools::compRelSEM(cfa_result, tau.eq = FALSE, ord.scale = TRUE),
  error = function(e) {
    cat("compRelSEM failed:", conditionMessage(e),
        "\nFalling back to semTools::reliability().\n")
    tryCatch({
      rel <- semTools::reliability(cfa_result)
      rel["omega3", ]
    }, error = function(e2) NULL)
  })

if (!is.null(omega_cat)) {
  cat("\nCategorical omega per factor (WLSMV solution):\n")
  print(round(omega_cat, 3))
  # Merge into the reliability table from Step 8
  idx <- match(names(omega_cat), reliability_table$Dimension)
  ok  <- !is.na(idx)
  reliability_table$Omega_cat[idx[ok]] <- round(as.numeric(omega_cat)[ok], 3)

  print(kable(reliability_table,   # [v3] explicit print()
              caption = "FINAL reliability table: ordinal alpha + categorical omega (use THIS in Table 2)",
              col.names = c("Dimension", "k items", "α ordinal",
                            "ω categorical (CFA)", "r_ii mean (poly)", "r_ii range (poly)"),
              align = "lrrrrl"))
} else {
  cat("\nOmega could not be computed — Table 2 of the manuscript must then be\n")
  cat("limited to ordinal alpha + CR, with Methods adjusted accordingly.\n")
}
```

## 10b. Discriminant Validity (Fornell-Larcker and HTMT)

```{r discriminant-validity}
lat_cors <- lavInspect(cfa_result, what = "cor.lv")
cat("Latent factor correlations:\n")
print(round(lat_cors, 3))
cat(sprintf("\nInterfactor correlation range (REPORT THIS in manuscript): r = %.3f – %.3f\n",
            min(lat_cors[lower.tri(lat_cors)]), max(lat_cors[lower.tri(lat_cors)])))

# Fornell-Larcker matrix: diagonal = sqrt(AVE) — print FULL 5x5 for Table S3
sqrt_ave  <- setNames(ave_cr_table$sqrt_AVE, ave_cr_table$Dimension)
fl_matrix <- lat_cors
diag(fl_matrix) <- sqrt_ave[rownames(fl_matrix)]

cat("\nFornell-Larcker matrix (FULL 5x5 — copy verbatim into Table S3,\n")
cat("including the Innovation diagonal):\n")
print(round(fl_matrix, 3))

# Explicit list of F-L violations (dynamic — no hard-coding)
fl_viol <- data.frame()
fn <- rownames(lat_cors)
for (i in seq_along(fn)) for (j in seq_along(fn)) {
  if (i < j) {
    r_ij <- lat_cors[i, j]
    if (r_ij > sqrt_ave[fn[i]] || r_ij > sqrt_ave[fn[j]]) {
      fl_viol <- rbind(fl_viol, data.frame(
        Pair = paste(fn[i], "-", fn[j]),
        r = round(r_ij, 3),
        sqrtAVE_1 = round(sqrt_ave[fn[i]], 3),
        sqrtAVE_2 = round(sqrt_ave[fn[j]], 3)))
    }
  }
}
if (nrow(fl_viol) > 0) {
  kable(fl_viol, caption = "Fornell-Larcker violations (report ALL in Table S3 note)",
        row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("\nFornell-Larcker criterion fully met.\n")
}

# [v2] HTMT on polychoric correlations (ordered), matching Methods
htmt_result <- tryCatch({
  semTools::htmt(model_5f, data = data_cfa, ordered = all_items)
}, error = function(e) {
  cat("HTMT (ordered) failed:", conditionMessage(e),
      "\nFalling back to Pearson HTMT — if used, Methods must say so.\n")
  tryCatch(semTools::htmt(model_5f, data = data_cfa), error = function(e2) NULL)
})

if (!is.null(htmt_result)) {
  cat("\nHTMT ratios (polychoric; threshold .85 strict / .90 permissive):\n")
  print(round(htmt_result, 3))
  ht <- htmt_result[lower.tri(htmt_result)]
  if (any(ht > .90, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    cat(sprintf("\nHTMT > .90 detected (max = %.3f). Interpret as partial discriminant\n",
                max(ht, na.rm = TRUE)))
    cat("validity; the manuscript's 'integrated continuum' interpretation applies.\n")
  }
}
```

# Step 12 — Alternative Model Comparison

```{r model-comparison}

  cat("'χ² escalado WLSMV' is now accurate. Do not mix with unscaled values.\n")
}
```

# Step 13 — Measurement Invariance by Sex (WLSMV / theta / Wu-Estabrook)

```{r invariance}
# [v2] Categorical invariance with semTools::measEq.syntax(), keeping the
# estimator consistent with the main CFA (WLSMV). Empty response categories
# per group are handled by COLLAPSING adjacent categories on affected items
# (documented below and to be described in Methods). The previous MLR
# sequence is retained only as a fallback (with explicit caution).

data_cfa_full <- datos[idx_cfa, ]

if ("Sexo" %in% names(data_cfa_full) && !all(is.na(data_cfa_full$Sexo))) {
  sex_table <- table(data_cfa_full$Sexo)
  groups_ok <- names(sex_table[sex_table >= 100])

  if (length(groups_ok) >= 2) {
    data_inv <- data_cfa_full %>%
      filter(Sexo %in% groups_ok) %>%
      .[, c("Sexo", all_items)]

    cat("Groups included (CFA subsample with declared sex — state this n in Methods):\n")
    print(table(data_inv$Sexo))

    # --- Detect and collapse empty categories per group --------------------
    collapsed_items <- character(0)
    for (it in all_items) {
      tab <- table(factor(data_inv[[it]], levels = 1:5), data_inv$Sexo)
      if (any(tab == 0)) {
        x <- data_inv[[it]]
        x <- ifelse(x <= 2, 2, x) - 1            # merge 1&2 -> categories 1..4
        tab2 <- table(factor(x, levels = 1:4), data_inv$Sexo)
        if (any(tab2 == 0)) x <- pmin(x, 3)      # merge top if still empty -> 1..3
        data_inv[[it]] <- x
        collapsed_items <- c(collapsed_items, it)
      }
    }
    if (length(collapsed_items) > 0) {
      cat(sprintf("\nCategories collapsed (bottom merge 1&2) on %d items:\n%s\n",
                  length(collapsed_items),
                  paste(collapsed_items, collapse = ", ")))
      cat("-> Describe this in Methods: 'response categories with zero frequency\n")
      cat("   in either sex group were merged with the adjacent category prior\n")
      cat("   to multigroup estimation'.\n")
    } else {
      cat("\nNo empty categories detected — no collapsing needed.\n")
    }

    # --- Wu & Estabrook (2016) sequence: configural -> thresholds -> loadings
    run_measEq <- function(geq) {
      tryCatch(
        semTools::measEq.syntax(
          configural.model = model_5f,
          data             = data_inv,
          ordered          = all_items,
          parameterization = "theta",
          ID.fac           = "std.lv",
          ID.cat           = "Wu.Estabrook.2016",
          group            = "Sexo",
          group.equal      = geq,
          return.fit       = TRUE,
          estimator        = "WLSMV"),
        error = function(e) { cat("measEq error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
    }

    fit_config <- run_measEq("configural")
    fit_thresh <- run_measEq("thresholds")
    fit_load   <- run_measEq(c("thresholds", "loadings"))

    inv_models <- Filter(Negate(is.null),
                         list("Configural"            = fit_config,
                              "Thresholds"            = fit_thresh,
                              "Thresholds + Loadings" = fit_load))

    if (length(inv_models) >= 2) {
      # Scaled indices for WLSMV
      inv_idx <- c("cfi.scaled", "tli.scaled", "rmsea.scaled", "srmr")
      inv_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(inv_models, function(m) {
        fit <- fitMeasures(m, inv_idx)
        data.frame(CFI   = round(fit["cfi.scaled"],   3),
                   TLI   = round(fit["tli.scaled"],   3),
                   RMSEA = round(fit["rmsea.scaled"], 3),
                   SRMR  = round(fit["srmr"],         3))
      }))
      inv_tab <- cbind(Model = names(inv_models), inv_tab)
      inv_tab$dCFI   <- c(NA, round(diff(inv_tab$CFI),   3))
      inv_tab$dRMSEA <- c(NA, round(diff(inv_tab$RMSEA), 3))

      print(kable(inv_tab,   # [v3] print() — was silently swallowed inside if{}
                  caption = "Measurement invariance — WLSMV, theta, Wu & Estabrook (2016) sequence",
                  row.names = FALSE))

      cat("\nCriterion: |dCFI| <= .010 and |dRMSEA| <= .015 (Chen, 2007;\n")
      cat("Putnick & Bornstein, 2016; Rutkowski & Svetina, 2017 for categorical).\n")

      if (inv_tab$CFI[1] < .90) {
        cat("\n*** CAUTION: configural CFI < .90. Invariance conclusions must be\n")
        cat("*** framed as TENTATIVE in the manuscript, and the configural misfit\n")
        cat("*** must be reported explicitly as a limitation.\n")
      } else {
        cat("\nConfigural baseline acceptable -> invariance sequence interpretable.\n")
        cat("Update Table S4 and the Results text with THESE values (the previous\n")
        cat("MLR-based table is superseded).\n")
      }
    } else {
      # ------------------- FALLBACK: previous MLR sequence ------------------
      cat("\nWLSMV invariance could not be estimated -> falling back to MLR.\n")
      cat("If this branch runs, the manuscript MUST (a) justify treating the\n")
      cat("items as continuous citing Rhemtulla et al. (2012), and (b) report\n")
      cat("the configural fit honestly, downgrading the conclusion if poor.\n\n")

      inv_configural <- tryCatch(
        cfa(model_5f, data = data_inv, group = "Sexo", estimator = "MLR"),
        error = function(e) NULL)
      inv_metric <- tryCatch(
        cfa(model_5f, data = data_inv, group = "Sexo", estimator = "MLR",
            group.equal = "loadings"),
        error = function(e) NULL)
      inv_scalar <- tryCatch(
        cfa(model_5f, data = data_inv, group = "Sexo", estimator = "MLR",
            group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts")),
        error = function(e) NULL)

      inv_models <- Filter(Negate(is.null),
                           list(Configural = inv_configural,
                                Metric     = inv_metric,
                                Scalar     = inv_scalar))
      if (length(inv_models) >= 2) {
        inv_idx <- c("cfi.robust", "tli.robust", "rmsea.robust", "srmr")
        inv_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(inv_models, function(m) {
          fit <- fitMeasures(m, inv_idx)
          data.frame(CFI   = round(fit["cfi.robust"],   3),
                     TLI   = round(fit["tli.robust"],   3),
                     RMSEA = round(fit["rmsea.robust"], 3),
                     SRMR  = round(fit["srmr"],         3))
        }))
        inv_tab <- cbind(Model = names(inv_models), inv_tab)
        inv_tab$dCFI   <- c(NA, round(diff(inv_tab$CFI),   3))
        inv_tab$dRMSEA <- c(NA, round(diff(inv_tab$RMSEA), 3))
        print(kable(inv_tab,   # [v3] print()
                    caption = "FALLBACK: invariance sequence — MLR (robust indices), by sex",
                    row.names = FALSE))
      }
    }
  }
}
```

# Step 14 — Criterion Validity

## 14a. Inter-dimension Correlations

```{r inter-dim-correlations}
datos_scores <- datos %>%
  mutate(
    Score_Knowledge   = rowMeans(.[, items_C], na.rm = TRUE),
    Score_Ethics      = rowMeans(.[, items_E], na.rm = TRUE),
    Score_Attitude    = rowMeans(.[, items_A], na.rm = TRUE),
    Score_Application = rowMeans(.[, items_P], na.rm = TRUE),
    Score_Innovation  = rowMeans(.[, items_I], na.rm = TRUE),
    Score_Total       = rowMeans(.[, all_items], na.rm = TRUE)
  )

scores_dim <- datos_scores[, grep("^Score_", names(datos_scores), value = TRUE)]
cor_dims   <- cor(scores_dim, use = "complete.obs")

cor_test_mat <- corr.test(scores_dim, use = "complete", adjust = "BH")

kable(round(cor_dims, 3),
      caption = "Inter-dimension correlation matrix (Pearson on mean scores)",
      align   = "rrrrrr")

cat("\nAll p-values (BH-adjusted for 15 simultaneous comparisons):\n")
print(round(cor_test_mat$p, 4))
```

## 14b. Concurrent Criterion Validity

```{r criterion-validity}
criterion_ok <- intersect(criterion_vars, names(datos))

if (length(criterion_ok) > 0) {
  data_criterion <- datos_scores[, c(grep("^Score_", names(datos_scores), value = TRUE),
                                     criterion_ok)]

  cor_crit <- cor(
    data_criterion[, grep("^Score_", names(data_criterion), value = TRUE)],
    data_criterion[, criterion_ok, drop = FALSE],
    use = "complete.obs"
  )
  print(kable(round(cor_crit, 3),   # [v3] print()
              caption = "Correlations between scale scores and criterion variables",
              align   = "rrr"))

  score_vars <- c("Score_Total", "Score_Knowledge", "Score_Ethics",
                  "Score_Attitude", "Score_Application", "Score_Innovation")
  crit_results <- data.frame()

  for (crit_var in criterion_ok) {
    for (score_var in score_vars) {
      ct <- cor.test(data_criterion[[score_var]], data_criterion[[crit_var]])
      crit_results <- rbind(crit_results, data.frame(
        Score     = gsub("Score_", "", score_var),
        Criterion = crit_var,
        r         = round(ct$estimate, 3),
        t         = round(ct$statistic, 2),
        df        = ct$parameter,
        p_raw     = ct$p.value
      ))
    }
  }

  crit_results$p_FDR <- round(p.adjust(crit_results$p_raw, method = "BH"), 4)
  crit_results$p_raw <- round(crit_results$p_raw, 4)
  crit_results$Sig   <- ifelse(crit_results$p_FDR < .05, "*", "")

  print(kable(crit_results[, c("Score","Criterion","r","t","df","p_raw","p_FDR","Sig")],   # [v3] print()
              caption = paste("Criterion validity: FDR-corrected correlations",
                              "(Benjamini & Hochberg, 1995) — 18 simultaneous comparisons"),
              row.names = FALSE))

  n_sig <- sum(crit_results$p_FDR < .05)
  cat(sprintf("\n* p_FDR < .05. Significant after FDR: %d / %d\n",
              n_sig, nrow(crit_results)))
  cat(sprintf("Range of r (for manuscript text): %.3f – %.3f\n",
              min(crit_results$r), max(crit_results$r)))

  # [v2] Ceiling-effect note computed from the data (criterion scale is 1–4)
  cat("\nCeiling-effect diagnostics (Likert 1-4):\n")
  for (v in criterion_ok) {
    x <- data_criterion[[v]]
    cat(sprintf("  %-13s observed range [%d, %d]; %% at top category (4) = %.1f%%\n",
                v, min(x, na.rm = TRUE), max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
                100 * mean(x == 4, na.rm = TRUE)))
  }
  cat("\nManuscript wording: 'concentration of responses in the top category\n")
  cat("(ceiling effect), which may attenuate the correlations'. DELETE any claim\n")
  cat("of 'total absence of responses in the top category'.\n")
}
```

```{r sociodemographics}
                            names(data_socio))
if (length(crit_vars_here) > 0) {
  crit_desc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(crit_vars_here, function(v) {

               Max = max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
               Pct_top = paste0(round(100 * mean(x == 4, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "%"))
  }))
  print(kable(crit_desc,   # [v3] print()
              caption = "Criterion variables — descriptive statistics (Pct_top = % at category 4)",
              row.names = FALSE))
}
```

```{r figura-afc, fig.width=14, fig.height=18, dpi=300, fig.cap="Figure 2. Standardized path diagram of the five-factor CFA model (values drawn dynamically from the fitted model)."}
# [v2] Loadings and factor correlations are now built DYNAMICALLY from
# std_sol and lat_cors — no hard-coded values that can drift from outputs.

factor_order <- c("Knowledge","Ethics","Attitude","Application","Innovation")
factor_labels <- c(Knowledge = "Knowledge", Ethics = "Ethics",
                  Attitude = "Attitude", Application = "Application",
                  Innovation = "Innovation")

factors <- data.frame(
  name = factor_order,
  x    = c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9),
  y    = rep(8, 5),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
factors$k     <- sapply(factor_order, function(f) sum(std_sol$Factor == f))
factors$label <- paste0(factor_labels[factors$name], "\n(", factors$k, " items)")

item_rows <- list()
for (fi in seq_len(nrow(factors))) {
  fname <- factors$name[fi]
  fx    <- factors$x[fi]
  sub   <- std_sol[std_sol$Factor == fname, ]
  n     <- nrow(sub)
  ys    <- seq(6.2, 0.2, length.out = n)
  item_rows[[fi]] <- data.frame(
    factor = fname,
    label  = gsub("^IA\\.", "", sub$Item),
    load   = sub$Std_loading,
    x      = fx,
    y      = ys,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
items_df <- do.call(rbind, item_rows)

fn <- factor_order
fcor <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(fn), function(i) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(fn), function(j) {
    if (i < j) data.frame(f1 = fn[i], f2 = fn[j],
                          r = round(lat_cors[fn[i], fn[j]], 3)) else NULL
  }))
}))
fcor <- merge(fcor, factors[, c("name","x","y")], by.x = "f1", by.y = "name")
names(fcor)[names(fcor) == "x"] <- "x1"; names(fcor)[names(fcor) == "y"] <- "y1"
fcor <- merge(fcor, factors[, c("name","x","y")], by.x = "f2", by.y = "name")
names(fcor)[names(fcor) == "x"] <- "x2"; names(fcor)[names(fcor) == "y"] <- "y2"
fcor$mx <- (fcor$x1 + fcor$x2) / 2
fcor$my <- (fcor$y1 + fcor$y2) / 2 + 0.6

pal_factor <- "#1B4F72"; pal_item <- "#AED6F1"
pal_load   <- "#2E86C1"; pal_cor  <- "#7F8C8D"

p_afc <- ggplot() +
  geom_curve(data = fcor,
             aes(x = x1, y = y1, xend = x2, yend = y2),
             curvature = -0.3, color = pal_cor,
             linewidth = 0.4, linetype = "dashed",
             arrow = arrow(ends = "both", length = unit(0.08, "inches"),
                           type = "open")) +
  geom_label(data = fcor,
             aes(x = mx, y = my, label = sprintf("%.2f", r)),
             size = 2.2, color = pal_cor, fill = "white",
             label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines"), label.size = 0) +
  geom_segment(data = items_df,
               aes(x = x, y = y + 0.18, xend = x, yend = 7.55),
               color = pal_load, linewidth = 0.35,
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.07, "inches"), type = "closed")) +
  geom_text(data = items_df,
            aes(x = x + 0.22, y = (y + 7.7) / 2, label = sprintf("%.2f", load)),
            size = 2.0, color = pal_load, hjust = 0) +
  geom_rect(data = items_df,
            aes(xmin = x - 0.38, xmax = x + 0.38,
                ymin = y - 0.16, ymax = y + 0.16),
            fill = pal_item, color = "#2980B9", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = items_df,
            aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
            size = 2.2, color = "#1A252F") +
  geom_ellipse(data = factors,
               aes(x0 = x, y0 = y, a = 0.65, b = 0.38, angle = 0),
               fill = pal_factor, color = "#154360",
               linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.92) +
  geom_text(data = factors,
            aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
            size = 2.8, color = "white", fontface = "bold",
            lineheight = 0.85) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.2, 10.2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.1, 9.5)) +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin     = margin(10, 10, 10, 10),
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0.5,
                                   margin = margin(b = 6)),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5, color = "#555555",
                                   margin = margin(b = 10))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Figure 2. Five-Factor CFA Path Diagram",
    subtitle = sprintf("Standardized loadings (WLSMV estimator, n_CFA = %d). All paths p < .001.",
                       nrow(data_cfa))
  )

print(p_afc)

ggsave("Figure2_CFA_PathDiagram.png", plot = p_afc,
       width = 14, height = 18, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
cat("Figure 2 saved: Figure2_CFA_PathDiagram.png\n")
```
